a HCI Researcher and Feminist in Taiwan

En-Kai (Debby) Chang

I'm a master's student at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taiwan, and a research assistant in the Critical Creative Computing Lab at National Cheng Kung University, advised by Prof. Ying-Yu Chen. Outside of research, I'm an amateur portrait photographer who loves hand-crafting and zine-making, and I bring that same hands-on, people-first curiosity into my work — grounded in a background in communication and multimedia, and a master's training in qualitative research.

My work focuses on how underrepresented communities make, share, and contest meaning through technology, and I love working closely and collaboratively with the communities I study. I use qualitative methodologies, including co-design, ethnography, and research-through-design, to study care, identity, and domestic life.

Going forward, I'm interested in developing creative, asset-based technologies that build on communities' existing strengths and ways of making.

About

Research focus

My research draws on critical social and communication theory to examine how technology shapes everyday life, and my experience with narrative and material media — zines, interactive interfaces, textile objects — has shaped my interest in using these as research tools. I bring this combination into critical computing and community-based design, working alongside underrepresented groups and families in non-Western contexts to understand how they make sense of, and push back against, the technologies shaping their lives.

Recent projects include supporting hermeneutical autonomy for LGBTQ+ people in Taiwan (CHI 2026), studying how families collectively make data with a shared domestic object to mediate care (TAICHI 2026 · Best Paper), and co-designing storytelling chatbots with Southeast Asian immigrant mothers (TAICHI 2025 · Honorable Mention). I'm preparing to apply to HCI PhD programs in Europe, hoping to extend this work — grounded in the qualitative and design-research methods I trained in as a research assistant, including research-through-design, co-design, and participatory design — toward questions of embodiment, gender, culture, and more-than-human relations in computing.

Current Work

Ongoing projects

Collaborator

Co-designing Storytelling Chatbots with Southeast Asian Immigrant Women

Advisor: Ying-Yu Chen, National Cheng Kung University

Co-design workshops on storytelling chatbots exploring how Southeast Asian immigrant women narrate their life stories within trustless and silencing social environments in Taiwan, followed by field deployment to inform design recommendations.

▶ Watch a project video of the storytelling co-design work
Co-Lead

Collective Data-Making for Family Care through a Domestic Object

Advisor: Yu-Ting Cheng, National Taiwan University of Science and Technology

A research-through-design project using a data-enabled design approach to extend prior work (TAICHI 2026, Best Paper) on how families and a shared domestic object collectively make and interpret data to mediate care relationships between members.

▶ Watch a short demo of the sofa in action
Project Lead

Short-Video Entrepreneurship Among Southeast Asian Immigrant Women in Taiwan

Advisor: Ying-Yu Chen, National Cheng Kung University

A critical computing study combining digital ethnography and interviews to examine how Southeast Asian immigrant women leverage personal assets to build entrepreneurial ventures on short-video platforms, and how they negotiate tensions between platform demands and domestic labor — surfacing design opportunities for platform design.

Experience & Service

Work & community

I care about staying close to the communities I study. Outside of my research, I volunteer directly with immigrant families in Hsinchu and help coordinate Taiwan's HCI community — work that keeps me grounded in the field and reflects how much I value hands-on, relationship-based collaboration.
